tools.name: mcp__plugin_linear_linear__list_comments
tools.description: List comments on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. Provide exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId`. For issues, projects, and initiatives this returns both top-level discussion threads and inline description comments. Inline (anchored) comments carry a non-null `quotedText` set to the snippet of description text they reference. Returned comments include `author` and nullable `onBehalfOf`; when set, `onBehalfOf` identifies the user the agent author acted for. Files uploaded in comment bodies are returned in `attachments` with titles and download URLs, not issue attachment IDs. Signed upload URLs expire after five minutes; call list_comments again to refresh them. Download documents using these URLs and process them with your own file tools.

tools.name: mcp__plugin_linear_linear__prepare_attachment_upload
tools.description:
Prepare a direct Linear file upload for an existing issue.

Workflow:
1. Call this tool with issue, filename, contentType, and size.
2. Upload raw bytes with PUT to uploadRequest.url outside MCP.
3. All headers in uploadRequest.headers are part of the signed request, so send them verbatim.
4. After PUT succeeds, call create_attachment_from_upload with assetUrl to link it to the issue.

Do not base64-encode or transform the file. Use curl --data-binary @path or fetch(url, { method: 'PUT', body: blob }).
Omitting or modifying any signed header, including casing, will return HTTP 403.
The signed URL must be used within 60 seconds or it will expire.

Upload sequencing:
Prepare, PUT, and finalize one file before calling this tool for another file.
Do not batch multiple prepare_attachment_upload calls before starting the PUTs because earlier signed URLs can expire while later files are prepared.

Example:
curl -X PUT --data-binary @file.png \
  -H "content-type: image/png" \
  -H "x-goog-content-length-range: N,N" \
  -H "cache-control: public, max-age=31536000" \
  -H 'Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="file.png"' \
  "<uploadRequest.url>"

tools.name: mcp__plugin_linear_linear__save_comment
tools.description: Create or update a comment on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. If `id` is provided, updates the existing comment; otherwise creates a new one. To start a new thread, pass `body` and exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId` — comments on issues/projects/initiatives become top-level discussion threads; comments on documents/milestones become description comments. A status update holds a single thread, so a comment on an update that already has one is added to it as a reply. To reply to an existing thread, pass `parentId` and `body`; the reply inherits the parent's thread type, so no entity reference is needed. Parent reference fields are ignored when `id` or `parentId` is provided (`statusUpdateType` is rejected instead).

If `id` is provided, updates the existing comment; otherwise creates a new one. To start a new thread, pass `body` and exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId` — comments on issues/projects/initiatives become top-level discussion threads; comments on documents/milestones become description comments. A status update holds a single thread, so a comment on an update that already has one is added to it as a reply. To reply to an existing thread, pass `parentId` and `body`; the reply inherits the parent's thread type, so no entity reference is needed. Parent reference fields are ignored when `id` or `parentId` is provided (`statusUpdateType` is rejected instead).

tools.name: mcp__stitch__create_design_system
tools.description:
Creates a new design system for a project. Use this tool when the user wants to set or update the overall visual theme, style, or branding of the application.
This includes configuring:
- Color Palette: Presets, custom primary colors, and saturation levels.
- Typography: Font families (e.g., Inter, Roboto, etc.).
- Shape: Corner roundness for UI elements.
- Appearance: Light and dark mode background colors.
- Design MD: Free-form design instructions in markdown.
This tool establishes the foundational design tokens that apply across all screens in the project.

**Instructions for Tool Call:**
*  Call `update_design_system` tool immediately after this tool to apply the design system to the project, and display the design system in the UI.

tools.name: mcp__stitch__generate_screen_from_text
tools.description:
Generates a new screen within a project from a text prompt.

**Instructions for Tool Call:**
*  This action can take a few minutes to complete. Please be patient. DO NOT RETRY.
*  If the tool fails with a timeout, don't retry. Instead, try to get the screen with `get_screen` method every 30 seconds for up to 10 times before giving up.
*  If the tool call fails due to connection error, the generation process may still succeed. Please try to get the screen with `get_screen` method later.

**Output:**
*  **`output_components`**: If `output_components` contains text, return it to the user. If `output_components` contains suggestions (e.g. "Yes, make them all"), present these suggestions to the user. If the user accepts one of the suggestions, call `generate_screen_from_text` again with `prompt` set to the accepted suggestion.

# TypeScript/JavaScript Coding Style

> This file extends [common/coding-style.md](../common/coding-style.md) with TypeScript/JavaScript specific content.

## Types and Interfaces

Use types to make public APIs, shared models, and component props explicit, readable, and reusable.

### Public APIs

- Add parameter and return types to exported functions, shared utilities, and public class methods
- Let TypeScript infer obvious local variable types
- Extract repeated inline object shapes into named types or interfaces

```typescript
// WRONG: Exported function without explicit types
export function formatUser(user) {
  return `${user.firstName} ${user.lastName}`
}

// CORRECT: Explicit types on public APIs
interface User {
  firstName: string
  lastName: string
}

export function formatUser(user: User): string {
  return `${user.firstName} ${user.lastName}`
}
```

### Interfaces vs. Type Aliases

- Use `interface` for object shapes that may be extended or implemented
- Use `type` for unions, intersections, tuples, mapped types, and utility types
- Prefer string literal unions over `enum` unless an `enum` is required for interoperability

```typescript
interface User {
  id: string
  email: string
}

type UserRole = 'admin' | 'member'
type UserWithRole = User & {
  role: UserRole
}
```

### Avoid `any`

- Avoid `any` in application code
- Use `unknown` for external or untrusted input, then narrow it safely
- Use generics when a value's type depends on the caller

```typescript
// WRONG: any removes type safety
function getErrorMessage(error: any) {
  return error.message
}

// CORRECT: unknown forces safe narrowing
function getErrorMessage(error: unknown): string {
  if (error instanceof Error) {
    return error.message
  }

  return 'Unexpected error'
}
```

### React Props

- Define component props with a named `interface` or `type`
- Type callback props explicitly
- Do not use `React.FC` unless there is a specific reason to do so

```typescript
interface User {
  id: string
  email: string
}

interface UserCardProps {
  user: User
  onSelect: (id: string) => void
}

function UserCard({ user, onSelect }: UserCardProps) {
  return <button onClick={() => onSelect(user.id)}>{user.email}</button>
}
```

### JavaScript Files

- In `.js` and `.jsx` files, use JSDoc when types improve clarity and a TypeScript migration is not practical
- Keep JSDoc aligned with runtime behavior

```javascript
/**
 * @param {{ firstName: string, lastName: string }} user
 * @returns {string}
 */
export function formatUser(user) {
  return `${user.firstName} ${user.lastName}`
}
```

## Immutability

Use spread operator for immutable updates:

```typescript
interface User {
  id: string
  name: string
}

// WRONG: Mutation
function updateUser(user: User, name: string): User {
  user.name = name // MUTATION!
  return user
}

// CORRECT: Immutability
function updateUser(user: Readonly<User>, name: string): User {
  return {
    ...user,
    name
  }
}
```

## Error Handling

Use async/await with try-catch and narrow unknown errors safely:

```typescript
interface User {
  id: string
  email: string
}

declare function riskyOperation(userId: string): Promise<User>

function getErrorMessage(error: unknown): string {
  if (error instanceof Error) {
    return error.message
  }

  return 'Unexpected error'
}

const logger = {
  error: (message: string, error: unknown) => {
    // Replace with your production logger (for example, pino or winston).
  }
}

async function loadUser(userId: string): Promise<User> {
  try {
    const result = await riskyOperation(userId)
    return result
  } catch (error: unknown) {
    logger.error('Operation failed', error)
    throw new Error(getErrorMessage(error))
  }
}
```

## Input Validation

Use Zod for schema-based validation and infer types from the schema:

```typescript
import { z } from 'zod'

const userSchema = z.object({
  email: z.string().email(),
  age: z.number().int().min(0).max(150)
})

type UserInput = z.infer<typeof userSchema>

const validated: UserInput = userSchema.parse(input)
```

## Console.log

- No `console.log` statements in production code
- Use proper logging libraries instead
- See hooks for automatic detection

</system-reminder>

# TypeScript/JavaScript Patterns

> This file extends [common/patterns.md](../common/patterns.md) with TypeScript/JavaScript specific content.

## API Response Format

```typescript
interface ApiResponse<T> {
  success: boolean
  data?: T
  error?: string
  meta?: {
    total: number
    page: number
    limit: number
  }
}
```

## Custom Hooks Pattern

```typescript
export function useDebounce<T>(value: T, delay: number): T {
  const [debouncedValue, setDebouncedValue] = useState<T>(value)

  useEffect(() => {
    const handler = setTimeout(() => setDebouncedValue(value), delay)
    return () => clearTimeout(handler)
  }, [value, delay])

  return debouncedValue
}
```

## Repository Pattern

```typescript
interface Repository<T> {
  findAll(filters?: Filters): Promise<T[]>
  findById(id: string): Promise<T | null>
  create(data: CreateDto): Promise<T>
  update(id: string, data: UpdateDto): Promise<T>
  delete(id: string): Promise<void>
}
```

content.content:
1	---
2	name: neatlogs-ts-langchain
3	description: Use when adding neatlogs observability to a TypeScript/Node.js project that uses LangChain or LangGraph (depends on `@langchain/*` / `@langchain/langgraph`).
4	metadata:
5	  author: neatlogs
6	  language: typescript
7	  framework: langchain
8	---
9	
10	# Neatlogs TypeScript Setup — LangChain / LangGraph
11	
12	This project uses LangChain (`@langchain/*`) or LangGraph (`@langchain/langgraph`). Neatlogs instruments it with **`langchainHandler()`** — a LangChain callback handler you attach via `{ callbacks: [handler] }`. This is the **only** supported path.
13	
14	> **`init({ instrumentations: ['langchain'] })` throws.** The OpenInference LangChain instrumentor creates and activates spans on the **global** OpenTelemetry context, which Neatlogs' private provider cannot isolate from a co-tenant tracer (Datadog, etc.), so `init()` rejects the key outright with a message pointing at `langchainHandler()`. Older guidance offered it as a zero-touch alternative — that is gone.
15	
16	## Core mechanism — `langchainHandler()`
17	
18	Create ONE handler and pass it via `{ callbacks: [handler] }` on the calls you want traced:
19	
20	```typescript
21	import { init, langchainHandler, span, flush, shutdown } from 'neatlogs';
22	import { ChatOpenAI } from '@langchain/openai';
23	
24	await init({ apiKey: process.env.NEATLOGS_API_KEY, workflowName: 'langchain-app' });
25	
26	const llm = new ChatOpenAI({ model: 'gpt-4o' });
27	
28	const handler = langchainHandler();
29	const res = await llm.invoke('Hello', { callbacks: [handler] });
30	```
31	
32	The handler is bound to Neatlogs' private provider, so import order doesn't matter — a static `import` of `@langchain/*` above `init()` is fine.
33	
34	### LangGraph: attach at the GRAPH invocation — NOT the per-node model call
35	
36	For LangGraph, attach the handler at the **graph invocation** (`app.invoke(...)` / `stream` / etc.), not on the per-node `llm.invoke()`. LangGraph fires the per-node `on_chain_start` only on the **graph-level callback manager**, so a handler passed to a single node's model call never sees the node boundaries — you get no node spans and the LLM span orphans to the workflow root (flat, no node hierarchy). Attach once at the graph invocation and each node gets its own span with the LLM nested under it.
37	
38	```typescript
39	async function analystNode(state) {
40	  const response = await llm.invoke(messages);                   // no per-node handler
41	  return { messages: [response] };
42	}
43	// ✅ attach at the graph invocation — nodes + nested LLMs all get spans
44	await app.invoke(state, { callbacks: [handler] });               // graph level ✅

name: neatlogs-ts-langchain
description: Use when adding neatlogs observability to a TypeScript/Node.js project that uses LangChain or LangGraph (depends on `@langchain/*` / `@langchain/langgraph`).
metadata:
  author: neatlogs
  language: typescript
  framework: langchain
---

# Neatlogs TypeScript Setup — LangChain / LangGraph

This project uses LangChain (`@langchain/*`) or LangGraph (`@langchain/langgraph`). Neatlogs instruments it with **`langchainHandler()`** — a LangChain callback handler you attach via `{ callbacks: [handler] }`. This is the **only** supported path.

> **`init({ instrumentations: ['langchain'] })` throws.** The OpenInference LangChain instrumentor creates and activates spans on the **global** OpenTelemetry context, which Neatlogs' private provider cannot isolate from a co-tenant tracer (Datadog, etc.), so `init()` rejects the key outright with a message pointing at `langchainHandler()`. Older guidance offered it as a zero-touch alternative — that is gone.

## Core mechanism — `langchainHandler()`

Create ONE handler and pass it via `{ callbacks: [handler] }` on the calls you want traced:

```typescript
import { init, langchainHandler, span, flush, shutdown } from 'neatlogs';
import { ChatOpenAI } from '@langchain/openai';

await init({ apiKey: process.env.NEATLOGS_API_KEY, workflowName: 'langchain-app' });

const llm = new ChatOpenAI({ model: 'gpt-4o' });

const handler = langchainHandler();
const res = await llm.invoke('Hello', { callbacks: [handler] });
```

The handler is bound to Neatlogs' private provider, so import order doesn't matter — a static `import` of `@langchain/*` above `init()` is fine.

### LangGraph: attach at the GRAPH invocation — NOT the per-node model call

For LangGraph, attach the handler at the **graph invocation** (`app.invoke(...)` / `stream` / etc.), not on the per-node `llm.invoke()`. LangGraph fires the per-node `on_chain_start` only on the **graph-level callback manager**, so a handler passed to a single node's model call never sees the node boundaries — you get no node spans and the LLM span orphans to the workflow root (flat, no node hierarchy). Attach once at the graph invocation and each node gets its own span with the LLM nested under it.

```typescript
async function analystNode(state) {
  const response = await llm.invoke(messages);                   // no per-node handler
  return { messages: [response] };
}
// ✅ attach at the graph invocation — nodes + nested LLMs all get spans
await app.invoke(state, { callbacks: [handler] });               // graph level ✅
// NOT: await llm.invoke(messages, { callbacks: [handler] });    // per-node ❌ (no node spans, LLM orphans)
```

(Plain LangChain — LCEL chains / bare `llm.invoke()` — is the opposite: attach per model/chain call as in the example above. The graph-level rule is LangGraph-specific.)

## What the handler captures (DO NOT manually wrap)

- Chat-model / LLM calls → LLM span (model, tokens, latency)
- Chain / node execution → CHAIN span
- LangChain tools → TOOL span
- Retrievers → RETRIEVER span

## Steps

1. **Install** → `references/1-install.md`
2. **Add init()** → `references/2-add-init.md`
3. **Set environment variables** → `references/3-set-env.md`
4. **Attach the handler; optionally add an app-owned WORKFLOW** → `references/4-add-workflow.md`
5. **Lifecycle (flush/shutdown)** → `references/5-lifecycle.md`

## Rules (apply to ALL steps)

- `await init(...)` runs once at startup. Import order does NOT matter — the handler binds to Neatlogs' private provider per call, so a static `import` of `@langchain/*` is fine (no dynamic `import()` needed).
- NEVER pass `instrumentations: ['langchain']` to `init()` — it **throws**. The callback handler is the only path.
- Create ONE `langchainHandler()` and pass it via `{ callbacks: [handler] }`. For plain LangChain (LCEL chains / bare model calls) attach per model/chain call. For LangGraph attach at the graph invocation (`app.invoke(..., { callbacks: [handler] })`), NOT the per-node `llm.invoke()`.
- The handler self-roots a parentless supported run. Add at most one app-owned `span({ kind:'WORKFLOW' })` only when the user-facing entry performs meaningful pre/post work or coordinates multiple runs.
- NEVER wrap individual chains, graph nodes, LangChain tools, or `llm.invoke()` with `span()`/`trace()` — they are auto-traced by the handler; manual wrapping duplicates.
- All lifecycle calls are async. Never hardcode API keys — use `process.env`.

1	# Reference: Next.js apps (App Router / API routes)
2	
3	If this project is a Next.js app, the key Next-specific requirement is initializing neatlogs from `instrumentation.ts` with a **dynamic import** (Step 1). Skipping it produces a 500 with `Module not found: Can't resolve 'crypto'` and NO traces.
4	
5	## 1. `init()` in `instrumentation.ts` via the `register()` hook — use a DYNAMIC import (REQUIRED)
6	
7	Next.js runs `register()` once at server startup — the right place for `init()`. Your route handlers then create a `langchainHandler()` and pass it via `{ callbacks: [handler] }`; LangChain imports in those routes can be plain static imports.
8	
9	**CRITICAL: import `neatlogs` dynamically *inside* `register()`, not at the top of the file.** A static top-level `import { init } from "neatlogs"` makes Next's instrumentation-layer bundler fail with `Can't resolve 'crypto'`, and `serverExternalPackages` does NOT cover the `instrumentation.ts` compilation. A dynamic `await import("neatlogs")` defers resolution to runtime. (This is a **bundler** constraint, not an instrumentation-ordering one.)
10	
11	```typescript
12	// src/instrumentation.ts
13	export async function register() {
14	  if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === "nodejs") {
15	    const { init, flush, shutdown } = await import("neatlogs"); // dynamic, not top-level
16	
17	    await init({
18	      apiKey: process.env.NEATLOGS_API_KEY ?? "",
19	      workflowName: "my-next-app",
20	      // NO instrumentations key — init() throws for "langchain".
21	    });
22	
23	    const gracefulShutdown = async () => {
24	      await flush();
25	      await shutdown();
26	      process.exit(0);
27	    };
28	    process.on("SIGTERM", gracefulShutdown);
29	    process.on("SIGINT", gracefulShutdown);
30	  }
31	}
32	```
33	
34	On Next 13/14 also set `experimental.instrumentationHook: true` (on by default in 15+).
35	
36	## 2. (Fallback) `serverExternalPackages` if a route still fails to bundle
37	
38	The dynamic import above is normally enough. If a route/server action statically imports the full `neatlogs` SDK and Next still errors with `Can't resolve 'crypto'`, mark it external:
39	
40	```typescript
41	const nextConfig = { serverExternalPackages: ["neatlogs"] };          // Next 15+

1	# Decorators and Traces Reference — NeatLogs TypeScript SDK
2	
3	Complete reference for all manual instrumentation APIs in the NeatLogs TypeScript SDK.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. `span()` Function Wrapper
8	
9	The primary manual instrumentation API for custom code. Wraps a function to create an OpenTelemetry span with NeatLogs-specific attributes.
10	
11	### Signature
12	
13	```typescript
14	import { span } from 'neatlogs';
15	import type { SpanOptions } from 'neatlogs';
16	
17	const wrapped = span(options: SpanOptions, fn: (...args) => any);
18	```
19	
20	### SpanOptions
21	
22	```typescript
23	interface SpanOptions {
24	  kind: SpanKind;           // Required: span kind
25	  name?: string;            // Span name (defaults to function name)
26	  description?: string;     // Human-readable description
27	  captureInput?: boolean;   // Serialize function args (default: true)
28	  captureOutput?: boolean;  // Serialize return value (default: true)
29	  mask?: MaskFunction;      // Per-span mask function
30	  internal?: boolean;       // Mark as internal span
31	
32	  // Agent-specific
33	  role?: string;            // AGENT: agent role
34	  goal?: string;            // AGENT: agent goal
35	
36	  // Tool-specific
37	  toolName?: string;        // TOOL/MCP_TOOL: tool name
38	  parameters?: Record<string, any>;  // TOOL: tool parameters
39	  toolJsonSchema?: Record<string, any>;  // MCP_TOOL: JSON schema
40	
41	  // Embedding-specific
42	  model?: string;           // EMBEDDING: model name
43	  dimension?: number;       // EMBEDDING: embedding dimension
44	}
45	```
46	
47	> **Note**: Unlike the Python SDK, the TypeScript `SpanOptions` does NOT have `captureStdout`, `tags`, or `version` fields.
48	
49	### Valid Kinds
50	
51	`span()` throws an `Error` for any kind not in this set:
52	
53	`WORKFLOW`, `AGENT`, `CHAIN`, `TOOL`, `RETRIEVER`, `EMBEDDING`, `GUARDRAIL`, `MCP_TOOL`
54	
55	### When to Use Each Kind
56	
57	#### WORKFLOW
58	
59	Top-level entry point that orchestrates the full pipeline.
60	
61	```typescript
62	import { span } from 'neatlogs';
63	
64	const runPipeline = span({ kind: 'WORKFLOW' }, async (topic: string) => {
65	  const analysis = await researcher(topic);
66	  const report = await writer(analysis);
67	  return report;
68	});
69	```
70	
71	#### AGENT
72	
73	Function representing an AI agent with a specific role/goal.
74	
75	```typescript
76	import { span } from 'neatlogs';
77	
78	const researcher = span(
79	  { kind: 'AGENT', name: 'researcher', role: 'Research Analyst', goal: 'Find relevant information' },
80	  async (topic: string) => {
81	    // ... agent logic with LLM calls ...
82	    return findings;
83	  },
84	);
85	```
86	
87	#### CHAIN
88	
89	Sequential processing step for intermediate processing or pipeline stages.
90	
91	```typescript
92	import { span } from 'neatlogs';
93	
94	const processDocuments = span({ kind: 'CHAIN' }, async (docs: string[]) => {
95	  return docs.map((d) => d.trim().toLowerCase());
96	});
97	```
98	
99	#### TOOL
100	
101	Tool/function call (web search, calculator, API call, etc.).
102	
103	```typescript
104	import { span } from 'neatlogs';
105	
106	const webSearch = span(
107	  { kind: 'TOOL', toolName: 'web_search', description: 'Search the web' },
108	  async (query: string) => {
109	    return await searchApi.search(query);
110	  },
111	);
112	```
113	
114	#### RETRIEVER
115	
116	RAG retrieval. Automatically extracts documents from the return value.
117	
118	```typescript
119	import { span } from 'neatlogs';
120	
121	const retrieveDocs = span({ kind: 'RETRIEVER' }, async (query: string) => {
122	  return await vectorDb.search(query, { topK: 5 });
123	});
124	```
125	
126	The RETRIEVER postprocessor automatically:
127	- Extracts the query from function args named `query`, `question`, or `text`
128	- Extracts documents from array results or objects with `documents`/`docs`/`results` keys
129	- Sets canonical `neatlogs.retriever.documents.N.{content,id,score,metadata}` attributes for every returned document; do not truncate results client-side
130	
131	#### EMBEDDING
132	
133	Embedding generation.
134	
135	```typescript
136	import { span } from 'neatlogs';
137	
138	const embedTexts = span(
139	  { kind: 'EMBEDDING', model: 'text-embedding-3-small', dimension: 1536 },
140	  async (texts: string[]) => {
141	    return await embeddingModel.encode(texts);
142	  },
143	);
144	```
145	
146	#### GUARDRAIL
147	
148	Input/output validation and safety checks.
149	
150	```typescript
151	import { span } from 'neatlogs';
152	
153	const checkToxicity = span({ kind: 'GUARDRAIL' }, async (text: string) => {
154	  const result = await toxicityModel.check(text);
155	  return { passed: result.score < 0.5, score: result.score };
156	});
157	```
158	
159	#### MCP_TOOL
160	
161	MCP protocol tool handlers. Automatically wraps string results as `{ result: "..." }` and extracts input from the first argument.
162	
163	```typescript
164	import { span } from 'neatlogs';
165	
166	const getWeather = span(
167	  { kind: 'MCP_TOOL', toolName: 'get_weather', description: 'Get current weather' },
168	  async (location: string) => {
169	    return `Weather in ${location}: Sunny, 72°F`;
170	  },
171	);
172	```
173	
174	### `captureInput` / `captureOutput`
175	
176	Default is `true` for both. Set to `false` to suppress serialization — useful for large payloads or sensitive data.
177	
178	```typescript
179	const processLargeFile = span(
180	  { kind: 'CHAIN', captureInput: false, captureOutput: false },
181	  async (data: Buffer) => { /* ... */ },
182	);
183	```
184	
185	### Complete Multi-Agent Example
186	
187	```typescript
188	import { init, wrapOpenAI, span, flush, shutdown } from 'neatlogs';
189	import { OpenAI } from 'openai';
190	
191	await init({
192	  apiKey: '...',
193	  workflowName: 'research-app',
194	});
195	
196	const client = wrapOpenAI(new OpenAI());
197	
198	const webSearch = span(
199	  { kind: 'TOOL', toolName: 'web_search' },
200	  async (query: string) => {
201	    return `Results for: ${query}`;
202	  },
203	);
204	
205	const researcher = span(
206	  { kind: 'AGENT', name: 'researcher', role: 'Research Analyst' },
207	  async (topic: string) => {
208	    const searchResults = await webSearch(topic);
209	    const response = await client.chat.completions.create({
210	      model: 'gpt-4o',
211	      messages: [{ role: 'user', content: `Analyze: ${searchResults}` }],
212	    });
213	    return response.choices[0].message.content;
214	  },
215	);
216	
217	const runPipeline = span({ kind: 'WORKFLOW' }, async (topic: string) => {
218	  return await researcher(topic);
219	});
220	
221	await runPipeline('quantum computing');
222	await flush();
223	await shutdown();
224	```
225	
226	---
227	
228	## 2. `Span()` Class Method Decorator
229	
230	TC39 Stage 3 class-method decorator variant of `span()`. Uses the same `SpanOptions`.
231	
232	```typescript
233	import { Span } from 'neatlogs';
234	
235	class ResearchAgent {
236	  @Span({ kind: 'AGENT', role: 'researcher' })
237	  async run(query: string) {
238	    // ... agent logic ...
239	    return findings;
240	  }
241	
242	  @Span({ kind: 'TOOL', toolName: 'summarize' })
243	  summarize(text: string) {
244	    return text.slice(0, 200);
245	  }
246	}
247	```
248	
249	> **Note**: The `Span()` decorator requires TypeScript 5.0+ with `experimentalDecorators` disabled (TC39 Stage 3 decorators). It is a `ClassMethodDecoratorContext` decorator.
250	
251	---
252	
253	## 3. `trace()` Callback Wrapper
254	
255	For unsupported/custom operations that need direct canonical span attributes.
256	Do not use `trace()` as a second LLM capture layer around a call
257	owned by a wrapper, handler, hook, processor, or instrumentor.
258	
259	### Signature
260	
261	```typescript
262	import { trace } from 'neatlogs';
263	import type { TraceOptions } from 'neatlogs';
264	
265	const result = await trace(options: TraceOptions, async (span) => {
266	  // user code runs here with the span active
267	  return value;
268	});
269	```
270	
271	### TraceOptions
272	
273	```typescript
274	interface TraceOptions {
275	  name: string;                  // Required: span name
276	  kind?: SpanKind;               // Span kind (default: 'CHAIN')
277	  mask?: MaskFunction;           // Per-trace mask function
278	  attributes?: Record<string, any>;  // Custom span attributes
279	}
280	```
281	
282	**IMPORTANT**: Unlike `span()`, `trace()` does NOT validate the kind string at runtime. It accepts extended values including `'LLM'`, `'RERANKER'`, and `'VECTOR_STORE'`, although the current `TraceOptions.kind` type is narrower; use `kind: 'LLM' as any` (or the corresponding extended kind) at that boundary. Use `'LLM'` only when this manual trace is the sole capture owner for an unsupported/raw call.
283	
284	When `kind` is not provided, it defaults to `'CHAIN'`.
285	
286	### Sessions & end-user
287	
288	Session and end-user identity are **per-request** and set at the **trace root** — never on `init()` (`init()` does NOT take `sessionId` / `autoSession`).
289	
290	Per turn, set them on the root `trace()` or `span()`:
291	
292	```typescript
293	await trace(
294	  { name: 'turn', sessionId: 'conv_123', endUserId: 'u_456', endUserMetadata: { plan: 'pro' } },
295	  async () => { /* this turn's work */ },
296	);
297	
298	// or on a root span:
299	await span({ kind: 'WORKFLOW', sessionId: 'conv_123', endUserId: 'u_456' }, fn)();
300	```
301	
302	Wrapper-only code (only `wrap(...)` calls, no manual root) uses `identify()` — the wrapper's auto-root inherits it:
303	
304	```typescript
305	await identify({ sessionId: 'conv_123', endUserId: 'u_456' }, async () => {
306	  /* wrapped LLM call */
307	});
308	```
309	
310	Reuse the same `sessionId` on every turn to group them into one session; the end-user is per session. Identity is **root-only** — set it once on the root and the backend rolls it up across the trace.
311	
312	### Span Object Methods
313	
314	The `span` parameter in the callback is an OpenTelemetry `Span`. Available methods:
315	
316	```typescript
317	await trace({ name: 'my_op', kind: 'CHAIN' }, async (span) => {
318	  span.setAttribute('key', 'value');        // Add a custom attribute
319	  span.recordException(error);               // Record an exception
320	  span.setStatus({ code: SpanStatusCode.ERROR, message: 'msg' });
321	  span.addEvent('event_name', { key: 'val' });
322	});
323	```
324	
325	### Use Cases for `trace()`
326	
327	1. **Custom attribute capture** — use `span.setAttribute()` inside the callback
328	2. **Unsupported/raw operations** — create a manual span only when no wrapper, callback, hook, processor, native telemetry, or provider instrumentor owns it
329	3. **Span kinds not available in `span()`**: `'LLM'`, `'RERANKER'`, `'VECTOR_STORE'`
330	
331	### Common Anti-Pattern
332	
333	Do NOT wrap a function that already uses `span({ kind: 'WORKFLOW' })` in `trace()` — it's redundant:
334	
335	```typescript
336	// ❌ WRONG: Redundant wrapper
337	const myWorkflow = span({ kind: 'WORKFLOW' }, async () => { /* ... */ });
338	await trace({ name: 'main' }, async () => {
339	  await myWorkflow();  // Already traced by span()
340	});
341	
342	// ✅ CORRECT: Just call it directly
343	await myWorkflow();
344	```
345	
346	---
347	
348	## 4. `log()` — Structured Logging
349	
350	Capture timestamped log steps within the current trace.
351	
352	### Signature
353	
354	```typescript
355	import { log } from 'neatlogs';
356	
357	log(msgTemplate: string, options?: Record<string, any>);
358	```
359	
360	### Usage
361	
362	```typescript
363	import { log } from 'neatlogs';
364	
365	log('Processing query: {query}', { query: 'What is TypeScript?', level: 'info' });
366	log('Retrieved {count} documents', { count: 5 });
367	```
368	
369	- `msgTemplate` uses `{key}` placeholders (single braces)
370	- `options` provides template variables and an optional `level` (default: `'info'`)
371	- Requires `captureLogs: true` in `init()` for OTel LogRecord emission
372	- In debug mode, logs are echoed to console
373	
374	---
375	
376	## 5. Combine orchestration with automatically captured calls
377	
378	Use `span()` to represent real custom orchestration. Call handler-owned operations directly inside it; do not add an LLM `trace()` around them. Use a manual LLM trace only for an unsupported/raw call outside LangChain.
379	
380	## 6. Custom Span Attributes via `trace()`
381	
382	`LLM` is root-eligible. Current manual APIs add one `WORKFLOW` parent when another semantic kind would otherwise be parentless; nested calls keep their real parent. The LangChain handler also self-roots its supported runs.
383	
384	Manual spans must use these exact canonical keys:
385	
386	| Kind | Exact canonical attributes |
387	|---|---|
388	| `LLM` | Required when available: `neatlogs.llm.provider`, `neatlogs.llm.model_name`, `neatlogs.llm.input_messages.{i}.role`, `neatlogs.llm.input_messages.{i}.content`, `neatlogs.llm.output_messages.{i}.role`, `neatlogs.llm.output_messages.{i}.content`, `neatlogs.llm.token_count.prompt`, `neatlogs.llm.token_count.completion`, `neatlogs.llm.token_count.total`. Also report `neatlogs.llm.system`, `neatlogs.llm.finish_reason` or `neatlogs.llm.stop_reason`, `neatlogs.llm.is_streaming`, `neatlogs.llm.temperature`, `neatlogs.llm.top_p`, `neatlogs.llm.top_k`, `neatlogs.llm.max_tokens`, and `neatlogs.llm.invocation_parameters` when known. |
389	| `RETRIEVER` | `neatlogs.retriever.query`, `neatlogs.retriever.top_k`, `neatlogs.retriever.documents.{i}`, `neatlogs.retriever.input`, `neatlogs.retriever.output` |
390	| `RERANKER` | `neatlogs.reranker.model_name`, `neatlogs.reranker.query`, `neatlogs.reranker.top_k`, `neatlogs.reranker.input_documents.{i}`, `neatlogs.reranker.output_documents.{i}`, `neatlogs.reranker.input`, `neatlogs.reranker.output` |

402	
403	async function rerank(query: string, docs: string[], topN = 3) {

410	    );

412	    reranked.forEach((doc, i) =>
413	      span.setAttribute(`neatlogs.reranker.output_documents.${i}`, JSON.stringify(doc)),
414	    );
415	    return reranked;
416	  });
417	}

425	async function upsertDocuments(indexName: string, docs: Document[]) {
426	  return await trace({ name: 'upsert_documents', kind: 'VECTOR_STORE' as any }, async (span) => {
427	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.db.system', 'custom_vector_db');
428	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.db.operation', 'upsert');

459	      body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'gpt-4o', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: prompt }] }),
460	    });
461	    if (!response.ok) throw new Error('LLM request failed: ' + response.status);
462	    const data = await response.json();

464	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.llm.output_messages.0.role', 'assistant');
465	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.llm.output_messages.0.content', data.choices?.[0]?.message?.content ?? '');
466	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.llm.token_count.prompt', data.usage.prompt_tokens);
